answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Chart printer bound atlas seal filed with the star-chart archive changes that arithmetic: each bound atlas is a measured meridian arc plus a guild signature, so a farm must print a hundred real charts by hand, so the umber for each fake is paid in the real world. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the walnut of those crossings is a bill no payout covers. The jetty is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
